page: Hetzner Cloud cpx11 is an entry-tier virtual server running on the QEMU hypervisor within Hetzner's Regular Purpose family. It provides two shared vCPUs based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor line clocked at 2.0 GHz. The allocation pairs two physical cores with single-threaded operation, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory is configured at 2.0 GB of system RAM, yielding approximately 0.98 GB per core, with no GPU hardware present. Local persistent storage is bundled via a 40 GB NVMe SSD.

Benchmark outcomes place the cpx11 primarily in the entry-level performance tier. Compute testing reflects its shared two-core baseline, with stress-ng single-core reaching 754.39 and multi-core yielding 1524.77, placing both in the lower 10 percent of recorded results. PassMark evaluations corroborate this profile, registering a CPU score of 4396.25, a cryptographic score of 2214.53, and a memory rating of 1048.73. Memory throughput ranges from 231.55 GB/sec for small 16 KB cached blocks down to 31.66 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 18.69 GB/sec for large block writes.

Application and synthetic workload metrics demonstrate modest throughput constrained by shared vCPU allocation and memory ceilings. Static web serving reaches 2.4 GB/sec, while in-memory Redis SET operations achieve 3.3 million operations per second. Decompression tests via bzip3 log 9.86 GB/sec on a single thread and 17.92 GB/sec across both cores. Small language model execution utilizing a 135M parameter model sustains prompt processing speeds of 303.29 tokens per second and text generation speeds of 120.03 tokens per second.

Given its constrained memory footprint and shared vCPU resources, the cpx11 is cost-effective for lightweight, non-critical background services. It is technically suitable for basic staging environments, lightweight microservices, small automated scripts, proxy routing, or auxiliary edge tasks where high compute parallelism and intensive memory bandwidth are not required.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx11 is an entry-level virtual instance featuring 2 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 2.0 GB of system memory, yielding roughly 0.98 GB per core, and includes a bundled 40 GB NVMe SSD for local storage, without discrete GPU acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, the cpx11 demonstrates modest execution speed, scoring 4396.25 on the PassMark CPU test, 1524.77 on multi-core stress-ng, and achieving 3.3 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Large block uncached memory throughput reaches 31.66 GB/sec read and 18.69 GB/sec write. With modest throughput and shared compute resources, the cpx11 provides budget-oriented infrastructure best suited for non-intensive workloads, including basic web proxies, entry-level CI/CD runner steps, small utility services, and lightweight development environments.
